clue.text: Snakes will increase, not decrease, say leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the five words before it are their opening letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A forecaster or economist insists that something will rise rather than fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snakes' looks like a noun for reptiles, but it is a verb: a river or road snakes, twisting along its way.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to follow a twisting course, the same verb as a path that bends and curves around.

clue.text: Card game the French see making a comeback in campaigning politician's itinerary

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game for four players
les is the plural form of 'the' in French

indicators.note: coming back means the word for see is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: A card player watches the French side stage a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns SPOT into TOPS. A whistle-stop tour is a fast campaign trip with brief visits to many small towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Electioneering candidates make a quick series of short visits to small towns, each a brief halt on the schedule.

clue.text: Food fan: I'm tucking into split

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: tucking into means placing the first piece within the word for split

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear in fabric
I'm gives the letters IM, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An enthusiast says they are tucking into a dish split between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like eating, which suits 'Food', but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, whatever sustains a living body when eaten.

clue.text: Femme fatale keeps heads of idiotic rich earls in tin

indicators.note: keeps means the symbol for tin holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

indicators.note: the heads of the three words that follow are their first letters

explanation.surface: A seductive woman holds on to some foolish wealthy noblemen in a can.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth sirens lured sailors to their deaths, so the word now names a dangerously alluring woman.

clue.text: Support doctor inhaling O2 as a way out

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

indicators.note: inhaling means the abbreviation for doctor takes the following letters in

parts.note: O2 read as letters is two Os

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a patient by giving supportive oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: O2 looks like the oxygen molecule; here it is simply the letter O twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear entrance offers an exit, and figuratively a back door is a sneaky means of escape or entry.

clue.text: Injured boss I'm carrying up mountain as living material

indicators.note: carrying means the jumbled letters hold the reversed mountain inside them
injured means the letters of boss and I'm are knocked out of shape

parts.note: I'm gives the letters IM, the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for mountain is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A hurt employer complains about having to haul himself up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' makes PLA; 'Injured' makes BIOSMS, which carries it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bioplasm is an old term for the substance of living cells, synonymous with protoplasm.

clue.text: Finale where nothing divides 100,500 by 1

indicators.note: divides means the zero splits the two numerals by sitting between them

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
D is the Roman numeral for 500
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
one is A, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle asks what happens when zero comes into a long division sum.
explanation.walkthrough: '100,500' reads as one large number but is two Roman numerals, C and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, its closing section.

clue.text: Clashing and not crashing around space station

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go about the station's abbreviation
crashing means the letters of and not collide into a new order

parts.note: the ISS is the International Space Station

explanation.surface: Something collides near the orbiting station, or narrowly avoids doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' turns AND NOT into DONANT, which is split around ISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissonant notes jar against each other, so the sound is harsh and discordant.

clue.text: Newspaper boy from Wales is unmarried

indicators.note: unmarried means the M, standing for married, is taken away

parts.note: Morgan is a common Welsh given name for a boy

explanation.surface: A Welsh lad who delivers papers is single.
explanation.walkthrough: M is a standard abbreviation for married, as in genealogy tables.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a periodical that speaks for a party or group, such as a party's official paper.

clue.text: The art of home improvement? Si!

parts.note: the clue's two letters are the interior of the word design, its middle pair

explanation.surface: A Spanish speaker enthusiastically agrees that decorating is an art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Si!' looks like Spanish for yes; read the answer as an instruction and you get the two middle letters of DESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning the decor and furnishing of rooms is the craft of making a house look better.

clue.text: Holy lady gets rescue dog right away — better when undressed?

indicators.note: right away means one R, for right, leaves the dog breed

parts.note: the St Bernard is the Alpine breed famed for mountain rescue

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer letters, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: A saintly woman wonders if a rescue dog would look better without its coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernadette of Lourdes saw visions of the Virgin Mary in 1858 and was canonised in 1933.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a canonised saint of the Catholic Church, so a sacred woman.

clue.text: Shape of unloaded trailer, one thrown into fire

indicators.note: unloaded means the trailer is emptied of its contents, leaving only its ends
thrown into means the letter for one is put inside the word for fire

parts.note: an ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth, as in inglenook
one is A, as in a single item

explanation.surface: An empty trailer is pushed into a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: INGLE is an old word for a fireplace fire, surviving in INGLENOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided figure is one of the basic flat geometric forms.

clue.text: 100 + 0 over 10, right? I'm licked

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: over means the number word is turned back to front

parts.note: the number ten written as a word

explanation.surface: Someone checks a sum and finds themselves defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm licked' looks like an admission of defeat; spoken by the answer, it says an ice-cream cone gets licked.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer cone holding ice cream is eaten by running the tongue over it, so it describes itself.

clue.text: One working out cries uncontrollably after river run

indicators.note: after means the scrambled letters follow the river and the run

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: uncontrollably means the letters of cries are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sobs helplessly after a gruelling run along the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: An exerciser is a person doing a workout, or a gym machine used for training.

clue.text: Vehicle has trouble in road reversing and parking? Cheat!

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters sit inside the reversed road abbreviation
reversing means the road abbreviation is read backwards
trouble means the letters of has are stirred into a new order

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A driver struggles to back into a parking space and is accused of foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes SHA and 'reversing' makes DR; the surface's 'reversing and parking' is driving talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who wins at cards by trickery.

clue.text: Royal breaking free — she initially sprints, then jogs

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of free are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A princess escapes her minders and goes for a run, sprinting before slowing to a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' makes EFRE. 'jogs' looks like running, the surface's sense, but means stirs, as one jogs a memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's memory is to prompt it, revive it, bring it back to life.

clue.text: Old cave unearthed by instant replay

indicators.note: unearthed by means the letters are dug out from the words that follow, sitting within them

explanation.surface: An ancient cavern was discovered thanks to a slow-motion television rerun.
explanation.definitionFit: Antre is an archaic, poetic word for a cavern, used by Shakespeare in Othello.

clue.text: Star who's the pick of the bunch?

definitions.meaning: the leading person, the boss or chief figure in a group

definitions.text: who's the pick of the bunch?
definitions.meaning: a playful reading: the finest fruit in a bunch of bananas, the one at the top

explanation.surface: A celebrity is asked which is the best of a selection.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for the most important person in an organisation, the leading figure.

clue.text: Teacher to express displeasure with men

parts.note: to tut is to click one's tongue in disapproval
OR, other ranks, means the soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster clicks his tongue at the lads in the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private instructor who gives lessons to one or a few pupils.

clue.text: It joins any pets, if playful

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a thing that joins, a noun sense

indicators.note: playful means the letters of the three words frolic into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone joins any animals that are in a frisky mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It joins' is a clause standing for a thing that joins: a fastener for cloth or nappies.
explanation.definitionFit: This bent fastener with a covered point clips two pieces of fabric together.

clue.text: District gets hard capital upfront

indicators.note: upfront means the city comes before the letter for hard

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A region secures difficult funding paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' and 'upfront' read as money paid in advance; capital is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a small local area served by one church, or a civil subdivision of a county.

clue.text: Lift beams, say

indicators.note: say means the word for beams is to be heard spoken

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to hoist the timber joists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like roof timbers, but here they are shafts of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to elevate it, hoisting it higher.

clue.text: Console warrior online using this?

definitions.meaning: a control panel with keys, such as an organ's or a computer's set of keys
someone who fights aggressive battles in internet comments is said to be a warrior armed with this device

explanation.surface: A video gamer battles online using a games console.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyed panel of controls on an instrument or computer is a console in the musical and technical sense.

clue.text: Britain's behind in US money

parts.note: Br is an abbreviation for Britain or British
ass is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Britain lags behind America in wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang brass means cash, as in 'where there's muck there's brass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal northern English slang for cash.

clue.text: Hard growth is essentially difficult

indicators.note: essentially means only the essence, the core, of the word for difficult is kept, its ends removed

parts.note: a thorny problem is a difficult one

explanation.surface: Firm development is fundamentally tough to achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A bony projection on an animal's head, like a rhino's, is a tough outgrowth.

clue.text: After comic opera, villager embraces hot bird

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the opera's title

parts.note: The Mikado is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera

indicators.note: embraces means the word for villager wraps round the letter for hot

parts.note: a peasant is a country villager
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: After a night at a light opera, a country dweller hugs a sexy bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado pheasant is a long-tailed game bird native to Taiwan.

clue.text: Reptiles get bad press biting man's head off

indicators.note: biting means the jumbled letters close their teeth round the beheaded man
bad means the letters of press are spoiled into a new order
head off means the first letter of the word for man is removed

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Snakes have a poor reputation for attacking a man and decapitating him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' makes SERPS and 'head off' leaves ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes are cold-blooded scaly creatures of the reptile class.

clue.text: Criminal nears noose

indicators.note: criminal means the letters of nears are corrupted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker comes close to the hangman's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a wire loop trap that tightens around an animal, much like a hangman's loop.
